summary.text: Old forester of Pieria who saw Hermes drive Apollo's cattle away — bribed with a cow to keep silence, he betrayed the secret when tested in another shape, and Mercury turned his perjured heart to the touchstone that betrays gold.

story.text: On the day of his birth Hermes slipped from his swaddling-bands, walked to Pieria, and stole fifty head from Apollo's herd. Only one witness saw the theft: an ancient forester called Battus, keeper of the wood and green pasture where the blooded mares of rich Neleus grazed.

Mercury distrusted him and led him aside, promising a cow if he would keep silence. The god returned in another guise, offering a bull and a cow for word of the herd, and the old man promptly betrayed the secret he had been paid to keep. Hermes turned his perjured heart to stone — the touchstone, which betrays gold as Battus betrayed his oath.
He must not be merged with Battus the founder of Cyrene — the Pierian witness to the cattle-theft and the colonist of Thera belong to different genealogies and different ages of myth.
